wiki_catalogs.name: Getting Started
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive getting started content for Laris, the AI-native business operating system for Indonesian F&B UMKM. Explain what Laris is, its core purpose of replacing notebooks and WhatsApp chats with a unified POS, inventory, purchasing, CRM, financial reporting, and AI copilot system. Document installation requirements including Node.js 22.18+, npm setup, and environment configuration. Provide step-by-step instructions for both local demo mode at /demo and cloud deployment with Supabase. Include detailed environment variable setup, Supabase project creation, migration execution order, and authentication configuration. Explain the difference between local demo data (Kopi Senja) and cloud workspaces. Address common setup issues and provide troubleshooting guidance for beginners while ensuring experienced developers can quickly get the system running.

wiki_catalogs.name: Voice Recognition System
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create detailed documentation for the voice recognition system in Laris. Explain the Web Speech API integration with Indonesian language support, microphone permissions handling, and real-time speech-to-text conversion. Document the voice input UI components, including start/stop controls, visual feedback, and error states. Detail the fallback mechanisms when browser speech recognition is unavailable, including manual text input alternatives. Explain audio processing, noise cancellation considerations, and performance optimization for mobile devices. Include implementation examples of voice command capture, transcription handling, and integration with the order parsing pipeline. Address browser compatibility issues, permission management, and accessibility considerations for voice interactions.

wiki_catalogs.name: Product Catalog
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive documentation for the Laris product catalog system. Explain the product data model including fields like name, price, category, image, and active status. Document the product browsing interface with category filtering, search functionality, and visual product cards. Detail the product lifecycle from creation to activation/deactivation. Include examples of adding new products, updating prices, managing categories, and handling product images. Explain how products integrate with the recipe system for inventory management. Address performance considerations for large catalogs and mobile-first design patterns used in the UI.

wiki_catalogs.name: Main Application Shell
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the main LarisApp component that serves as the central container for the entire application. Document the component architecture including state management patterns, navigation system with hash-based routing, modal system with accessibility features, and view switching logic. Explain the dual-mode operation supporting both local demo mode with localStorage persistence and cloud mode with Supabase integration. Detail the responsive design patterns, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+K for search, Escape for closing), and mobile-first UI considerations. Include practical examples of how the component manages business state, handles user interactions, and coordinates between different feature modules. Address performance optimizations like useMemo for computed values and useCallback for event handlers.

wiki_catalogs.name: Raw Materials Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive documentation for the raw materials management system in Laris. Explain the InventoryItem interface structure including fields like id, name, unit, openingStock, reorderPoint, cost, and supplier. Document how raw materials are defined with Indonesian coffee shop examples like 'Biji kopi house blend' (beans), 'Susu segar' (milk), and 'Sirup gula aren' (palm sugar syrup). Detail unit conversion handling between grams, milliliters, pieces, and tea bags. Explain supplier relationship management and cost tracking mechanisms. Include practical examples of adding new raw materials, setting reorder points for low-stock alerts, and managing supplier information. Document the integration with purchasing workflows and how raw material costs affect product pricing calculations.

wiki_catalogs.name: Manual Purchase Entry
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the manual purchase entry system in Laris. Explain the complete workflow from opening the purchase modal to completing a transaction. Document the form fields including item selection dropdown, quantity input, total cost calculation, and date tracking. Detail the validation rules for numeric inputs, required fields, and business logic constraints. Explain how the system handles different inventory items and their units of measurement. Include practical examples of creating purchase records for raw materials like coffee beans, milk, and sugar. Document the integration with inventory management where purchases automatically update stock levels. Address error handling scenarios such as invalid quantities, missing items, and network failures. Explain the difference between local and cloud modes in purchase processing.

wiki_catalogs.name: Customer Profiles
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive documentation for the customer profile management system in Laris. Detail the Customer interface structure including id, name, phone, visits, totalSpent, lastVisit, segment, and points fields. Explain customer creation during sales transactions, automatic profile updates with visit tracking and spending accumulation. Document contact information validation including Indonesian phone number format handling (+84-15 digits). Cover customer lookup functionality by phone number matching with normalization (removing leading +). Include examples of customer profile data structures, search operations, and integration with the POS system. Address privacy considerations for storing customer contact information and compliance with Indonesian data protection regulations.

wiki_catalogs.name: Role-Based Access Control

Explain how roles are defined in the TeamMember interface and enforced throughout the application. Document the permission checking mechanisms that control access to different features like inventory management, financial reports, and team administration. Include concrete examples of role assignment workflows, permission validation functions, and security boundaries between roles. Address privilege escalation prevention, role inheritance patterns, and integration with Row-Level Security policies for database-level access control.

wiki_catalogs.name: Revenue Tracking
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create detailed documentation for the revenue tracking system in Laris. Explain how daily sales summaries are generated from the Sale interface, including subtotal, discount, tax, and total calculations. Document revenue trend analysis across different time periods (daily, weekly, monthly) and channel breakdown reporting between 'Kasir' (cashier) and 'Etalase' (display) channels. Detail the payment method breakdown showing QRIS, Tunai (cash), and Transfer distributions. Include practical examples of revenue calculation functions, date range filtering, and performance metrics like average transaction value and conversion rates. Document the integration with the deterministic seed data generator that creates realistic 90-day sales history for demonstration purposes.

wiki_catalogs.name: RFM Segmentation System

Document the migration strategy for adding new tables to the multi-tenant architecture and ensuring consistent policy application.

<blog>

# Laris — AI-Native Business OS for Indonesian UMKM

## 1. Project Introduction

**Laris** is a Next.js application built for the GTNIC 2026 hackathon that targets Indonesian micro, small, and medium food-and-beverage businesses (UMKM). Its purpose is to replace notebooks, WhatsApp chats, and scattered spreadsheets with one mobile-first system combining POS, recipe-level inventory, purchasing, CRM, an online storefront, financial reports, and an AI copilot called **Tanya Laris**.

The project’s core goals are:

- Record a sale in under five seconds through voice, text, or tap.
- Deduct raw-material stock automatically from recipes (BOM) so owners never run out of key ingredients at peak hours.
- Let owners ask natural-language questions about revenue, margins, low stock, and top products.
- Provide SAK EMKM-style financial statements and a self-assessed financing-readiness score.
- Ship a competition-ready demo within 23 days while keeping every feature usable without AI.

The target audience includes warung owners, coffee shop operators, caterers, bakeries, and their cashiers — users who prefer voice, photos, and WhatsApp over complex forms.

## 2. Technical Architecture

### Component Breakdown

The project follows a modern Next.js 15 App Router layout with clear separation between client UI, server actions, API routes, shared business logic, and Supabase-backed data.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Client[Next.js Client] --> Layout[Root Layout & Metadata]
  Client --> App[LarisApp Shell]
  App --> Views[POS / Transactions / Products / Inventory / Purchases / Customers / Storefront / Finance / Team]
  App --> Modals[Checkout / Receipt / Purchase / Settings / Product Editor / Forecast / Customer / Invite]
  App --> LocalData[laris-data.ts]
  App --> ServerActions[app/actions.ts]
  App --> AIAPI[/api/ai/*]
  AIAPI --> GoogleAI[Google Gemini via Vercel AI SDK]
  ServerActions --> Supabase[Supabase Postgres + RLS]
  Supabase --> Migrations[supabase/migrations]
```

### Design Patterns

| Pattern | Where It Appears | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Mode-based rendering** | `laris-app.tsx` | Runs fully locally in development/demo mode and switches to cloud mode when Supabase is configured. |
| **Server Actions** | `app/actions.ts` | Handles mutations like sales, purchases, expenses, customers, settings, and team invites. |
| **Route Handlers** | `src/app/api/ai/*` | Expose structured AI features: order parsing, receipt scanning, and Tanya Laris. |
| **Deterministic state functions** | `laris-data.ts` | Pure functions for cart totals, sales completion, purchase recording, stock calculation, and CSV export. |
| **Ledger-style stock tracking** | Database schema and `getStock` | Stock is never overwritten; it accumulates through `stock_movements`. |
| **Idempotency keys** | Checkout and purchase flows | Prevent duplicate transactions on retry. |
| **Zod validation** | API routes and server actions | Enforce request contracts before touching business logic. |
| **Multi-tenancy with RLS** | Supabase schema | Every tenant table carries `business_id`; Row-Level Security isolates tenants. |

### System Relationships

```mermaid
graph LR
  Browser[Browser / PWA] --> NextJS[Next.js App Router]
  NextJS --> ReactClient[React Components]
  NextJS --> ServerActions[Server Actions]
  NextJS --> APIRoutes[AI Route Handlers]
  APIRoutes --> AISDK[Vercel AI SDK]
  AISDK --> Gemini[Google Gemini]
  ServerActions --> SupabaseClient[Supabase JS Client]
  SupabaseClient --> Postgres[(Postgres)]
  Postgres --> RLS[Row-Level Security]
```

### Data Flow Diagrams

#### Golden Demo Path

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Cashier as Kasir
  participant POS as Laris POS
  participant AI as LLM
  participant DB as Supabase
  participant Owner as Owner (WhatsApp)

  Cashier->>POS: "Dua es kopsu less sugar, satu croissant, bayar QRIS"
  POS->>AI: Transcript + menu catalog
  AI-->>POS: Structured cart + payment method
  POS->>Cashier: Confirmation card
  Cashier->>POS: Confirm
  POS->>DB: Create order, payment, stock movements
  DB-->>POS: Success
  POS->>Owner: Low-stock alert → draft PO via WhatsApp
```

#### Sales Completion Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start[User completes checkout] --> Validate[Validate cart, payment, customer phone]
  Validate --> Calculate[Calculate subtotal, discount, tax, total]
  Calculate --> Recipe[Aggregate recipe requirements]
  Recipe --> CheckStock[Check available stock per ingredient]
  CheckStock --> Valid{Stock sufficient?}
  Valid -->|No| Error[Throw error with missing item]
  Valid -->|Yes| CreateSale[Create sale record]
  CreateSale --> UpdateCustomer[Update or create customer]
  UpdateCustomer --> Movements[Create stock movement ledger entries]
  Movements --> Persist[Persist to local state or Supabase]
  Persist --> Receipt[Show receipt modal]
```

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/app/layout.tsx` | Root layout, metadata, Jakarta Sans font, accessibility skip link. |
| `src/app/page.tsx` | Home route that redirects unauthenticated users, loads a Supabase snapshot, and renders `LarisApp`. |
| `src/components/laris-app.tsx` | Single large client component acting as the app shell, navigation, modals, POS, dashboard, and all major screens. |
| `package.json` | Defines Next.js 15, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Supabase, Vercel AI SDK, Zod, and dev tooling. |

### Core Modules

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Domain model, demo data, deterministic seed, cart math, sales completion, purchase recording, stock ledger, order parser, and CSV export. |
| `src/lib/env.ts` | Environment configuration helper used by the root page to decide whether cloud mode is available. |
| `src/lib/repo.ts` | Snapshot loading and role type definitions for cloud mode. |
| `src/app/actions.ts` | Server Actions for completing sales, recording purchases, adding expenses, saving products/inventory, inviting team members, and updating settings. |
| `src/middleware.ts` | Next.js middleware for authentication and routing protection. |

### Configuration Approach

Configuration is split across several layers:

- **Runtime environment**: `src/lib/env.ts` checks whether Supabase credentials are configured.
- **Build-time configuration**: `next.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`, and `postcss.config.mjs`.
- **Database migrations**: `supabase/migrations/*.sql` define the production schema, RLS policies, functions, workspaces, and hardening steps.
- **Demo configuration**: `DEMO_DATE = "2026-10-18"` anchors the deterministic seed data.

Key configuration files:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | Dependencies, scripts, and build commands. |
| `next.config.ts` | Next.js runtime and bundling configuration. |
| `tsconfig.json` | TypeScript compiler options. |
| `eslint.config.mjs` | Linting rules for the Next.js project. |
| `postcss.config.mjs` | Tailwind CSS processing. |
| `supabase/migrations/0001_schema.sql` | Core database schema with tenancy, catalog, inventory, sales, payments, stock ledger, purchases, expenses, audit log, AI telemetry, and holiday calendar. |

### External Dependencies

```mermaid
graph TD
  NextJS[Next.js 15] --> React[React 19]
  NextJS --> Tailwind[Tailwind CSS v4]
  NextJS --> SupabaseSSR[@supabase/ssr]
  NextJS --> SupabaseJS[@supabase/supabase-js]
  NextJS --> AISDK[ai SDK]
  AISDK --> GoogleAI["@ai-sdk/google"]
  NextJS --> Lucide[lucide-react icons]
  NextJS --> Zod[zod validation]
  NextJS --> ServerOnly[server-only]
```

Critical dependencies include:

- **Next.js 15** with Turbopack for development and builds.
- **React 19** for the client-side UI.
- **Supabase** for authentication, Postgres, storage, and realtime capabilities.
- **Vercel AI SDK** with Google Gemini integration for structured outputs.
- **Zod** for request validation.
- **Tailwind CSS v4** for styling.

### Integration Points

| Integration | Location | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Supabase Auth** | `src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`, `src/app/login/actions.ts` | Handles OAuth callback and sign-in/sign-out. |
| **Supabase Database** | `src/app/actions.ts`, `src/lib/repo.ts` | Reads/writes business data with RLS isolation. |
| **Google Gemini** | `src/app/api/ai/ask/route.ts`, `src/app/api/ai/parse-order/route.ts`, `src/app/api/ai/scan-receipt/route.ts` | Parses orders, scans receipts, and powers Tanya Laris. |
| **Local Storage** | `src/components/laris-app.tsx` | Persists `BusinessState` in demo/local mode. |
| **Speech Recognition** | `src/components/laris-app.tsx` | Uses Web Speech API (`id-ID`) for voice input with fallbacks. |
| **CSV Export** | `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Generates safe Excel-compatible sales exports. |

### Component Relationship Diagram

```mermaid
classDiagram
  LarisApp <|-- Home
  LarisApp --> LarisVisuals
  LarisApp --> LarisData
  LarisApp --> ServerActions
  LarisApp --> Modals
    Modals --> CheckoutModal
    Modals --> ReceiptModal
    Modals --> PurchaseModal
    Modals --> SettingsModal
    Modals --> ProductEditorModal
    Modals --> InventoryEditorModal
    Modals --> CustomerModal
    Modals --> InviteModal
  LarisVisuals --> RevenueChart
  LarisVisuals --> Sparkline
  LarisVisuals --> Trend
  LarisVisuals --> AiBadge
  LarisVisuals --> CafeIllustration
  LarisVisuals --> EmptyState
  LarisVisuals --> LarisMark
```

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview

Laris implements a subset of its PRD scope focused on the most impactful demo path:

1. **Onboarding & Multi-Tenancy** — Sign-up, workspace creation, guided setup, and tenant isolation.
2. **POS (Kasir)** — Product grid, cart, discounts, optional tax, cash and QRIS payments, digital receipt, and shift-aware operations.
3. **Voice & Chat Input** — Web Speech API transcript plus regex-based order parsing, with an AI-powered fallback.
4. **Inventory & Recipes** — Raw materials, BOM per product, automatic stock deduction, moving-average cost updates, and reorder alerts.
5. **Purchasing & Receipt Scan** — Manual purchase entry and multimodal receipt scanning with price-hike alerts.
6. **Customers & CRM** — Phone-based profiles, visit tracking, spending totals, RFM segmentation, and points.
7. **Online Storefront** — Public-facing menu and order channel.
8. **Financial Reports** — Revenue, gross margin, expenses, and basic financial views.
9. **Team & Access** — Roles including owner, manager, cashier, and kitchen staff.
10. **Tanya Laris Copilot** — Natural-language Q&A backed by tools over whitelisted data access.

### Implementation Highlights

| Feature | Key File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic 90-day seed data | `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Creates realistic sales, expenses, and customer history ending on `DEMO_DATE`. |
| Voice-to-cart parsing | `src/components/laris-app.tsx` | Supports colloquial Indonesian terms like *kopsu*, *goceng*, *ceban*, and modifiers like *less sugar*. |
| AI order parsing | `src/app/api/ai/parse-order/route.ts` | Sends transcripts to Gemini for structured JSON output. |
| Receipt scanning | `src/app/api/ai/scan-receipt/route.ts` | Multimodal OCR with fuzzy matching and price-hike detection. |
| Tanya Laris tools | `src/app/api/ai/ask/route.ts` | Tool-calling API for revenue, profit, top products, low stock, customer segments, and expenses. |
| Atomic stock deduction | `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Aggregates recipe needs before creating ledger entries. |
| Moving-average cost | `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Updates ingredient cost after purchases and recalculates product HPP. |
| RFM segmentation | `src/lib/laris-data.ts` | Classifies customers as Juara, Setia, Potensial, Berisiko, or Hilang. |
| Idempotent mutations | `src/components/laris-app.tsx`, `src/app/actions.ts` | Prevents duplicate sales and purchases on retry. |

### Feature State Diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> CartOpen: Add items
  CartOpen --> PaymentSelected: Review cart
  PaymentSelected --> Processing: Submit
  Processing --> Success: Valid transaction
  Processing --> Error: Validation failure
  Success --> Receipt: Show receipt
  Receipt --> Idle: Close receipt
  Error --> CartOpen: Fix input
  Idle --> VoiceInput: Tap microphone
  VoiceInput --> Parsing: Transcript received
  Parsing --> CartOpen: Confirmed items
  Parsing --> Error: Unknown items
```

## 5. Conclusion and Recommendations

### Summary

Laris is a well-scoped, demo-oriented Next.js application that combines a practical POS workflow with AI-assisted ordering, receipt scanning, and natural-language business insights. Its architecture cleanly separates client UI, server actions, AI APIs, and Supabase-backed data, while maintaining a fully functional local mode for development and judging.

Key architectural strengths include:

- Clear separation between local demo mode and cloud mode.
- Deterministic, auditable business logic in pure functions.
- Ledger-style stock tracking instead of direct quantity mutation.
- Strong validation using Zod and explicit domain types.
- Multi-tenant database design with RLS-ready tables.
- Graceful degradation: AI features fall back to local rules and manual UI.

### Potential Improvement Areas

1. **Component decomposition** — `laris-app.tsx` is very large and contains many views and modals. Splitting it into smaller route-scoped components would improve maintainability.
2. **Error boundary coverage** — Adding React error boundaries around critical sections would improve resilience during development and production.
3. **Testing expansion** — The current test script runs only `laris-data.test.ts`. Expanding tests to cover server actions, API routes, and critical UI flows would strengthen confidence.
4. **Environment documentation** — Adding a `.env.example` file would make local setup clearer for contributors.
5. **Accessibility audit** — While the layout includes a skip link, a full WCAG audit across all modals and POS interactions would be valuable.
6. **Performance profiling** — Measuring LCP, FID, and CLS on mobile devices would help validate the performance targets in the PRD.

### Actionable Recommendations

- Extract each major view (`overview`, `pos`, `transactions`, `products`, `inventory`, `purchases`, `customers`, `storefront`, `finance`, `team`) into its own page or component module.
- Move modal implementations into dedicated files rather than inline JSX inside the main app component.
- Add Playwright or Cypress tests for the golden demo path.
- Document required environment variables and provide a seeded demo account for judges.
- Introduce feature flags for AI-dependent features so the app can be tested offline more reliably.
- Add structured logging for AI calls beyond telemetry, including prompt/response snapshots for evaluation.

### Next Steps

1. Finalize the competition submission path and verify all links from an incognito window.
2. Run the golden demo end-to-end daily until submission.
3. Harden cross-browser compatibility, especially Safari and Firefox speech recognition fallbacks.
4. Prepare the proposal, video demo, and judge experience materials described in the PRD.
5. After submission, prioritize production QRIS integration, real-time order queue improvements, and expanded AI tool coverage.

</blog>
